The Claude Code bird, installed the way Claude Code installs things.

## As a plugin

```
/plugin marketplace add thousandflowers/canary
/plugin install canary@canary
```

That is the whole install for anyone who only ever wanted the status line
bird. The next session start finds the binary, or builds it from source when
Go is around and fetches the release binary otherwise, and wires the status
line. The shell rc is never touched.

A plugin cannot declare a status line: Claude Code's plugin manifest has no
field for one. So the plugin is one `SessionStart` hook that runs `canary
settings install`, which refuses to wire itself twice, and every session after
the first is a no-op that says nothing. The hook adds nothing to the model's
context. `canary` is the marketplace and `canary` is the plugin, hence
`canary@canary`.

`/plugin uninstall canary@canary` and `canary settings remove` take it back out.

## Why this exists

Run the one-liner a second time without `CANARY_CLAUDE_ONLY=1` and the shell
bird comes back, because the installer does what it is told. The plugin is the
install that cannot make that mistake: there is no shell half to wire.

## Also

Release CI now refuses a tag whose version the plugin manifest does not agree
with. The plugin installs straight from the repository, so a manifest left
behind is what its users would see.
